title: Linking through unique identifier in location history
description: Location history data stored in DS2 likely contains unique identifiers (user IDs, device IDs, session IDs) that can be used to link data records to specific individuals across different sessions and contexts.

title: Quasi-identifier combining in location history
description: Location history data contains combinations of attributes (timestamps, locations, movement patterns) that can serve as quasi-identifiers, potentially allowing re-identification of individuals when combined with other data sources.

title: Profiling an individual through location pattern analysis
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) derives daily routine and movement patterns from location history, which constitutes profiling an individual based on their behavioral data and location patterns.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The data flow involves processing identified location history data that is directly associated with specific data subjects.

title: Processing of identifier data in location history
description: Location history data contains unique references to the identity of data subjects through user identifiers, device identifiers, or session identifiers embedded in the stored data.

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Location history data contains revealing attributes such as home/work locations, movement patterns, and routine behaviors that support identification of the data subject.

title: Sensitive location data type collected
description: Location history is highly sensitive personal data that reveals detailed information about individuals' movements, routines, and potentially sensitive locations (home, workplace, healthcare facilities).

title: Excessive volume of location data processed
description: The flow involves querying location history 'across sessions', which may process an excessive amount of historical location data beyond what is functionally needed for deriving daily routine patterns.

title: Unnecessary analysis and enrichment of location data
description: The analytics service performs additional processing (pattern derivation, routine analysis) on location data that may go beyond what is strictly necessary for the stated functional goal.

title: Unawareness of location history processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their location history is being queried and analyzed across sessions to derive movement patterns and daily routines.

title: Lack of control over location data processing preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or provide consent regarding how their location history is processed, analyzed, and what patterns are derived from it.

title: Lack of control over rectification/erasure of location data
description: Data subjects may lack the ability to rectify incorrect location data or remove location history that is no longer relevant to the analytics purpose.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing location history 'across sessions' may violate the data minimization principle by collecting and processing more personal data than actually needed for deriving daily routine patterns.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Location history stored in DS2 may be retained longer than functionally needed, as historical location data across multiple sessions is processed for pattern derivation.

title: Profiling individual through inferred health conditions

assumptions: The app has access to sufficient historical health data to perform meaningful inference

title: Quasi-identifier combination through health indicators
description: Health condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) combined with other user attributes could serve as quasi-identifiers that link data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Health indicators are combined with other user data that could be used for re-identification

title: Revealing health attributes disclosed to user
description: The dashboard displays revealing health attributes (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) that directly identify the user's health status and condition.
assumptions: Health condition indicators are considered revealing personal attributes

title: Processing of identified health data
description: The app processes identified health data to generate and display condition indicators to the user.
assumptions: The system processes data that is linked to specific identified users

title: Sensitive health data types disclosed
description: The app displays highly sensitive health data (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) which may be more sensitive than functionally required for basic app functionality.
assumptions: Health risk indicators are considered sensitive personal data under privacy regulations

title: Unnecessary data analysis and enrichment
description: The app performs analysis and enrichment of health data to create risk signals, which may exceed what is functionally necessary for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: The inference/analysis of health conditions may not be strictly necessary for basic app operation

title: User unawareness of health data processing
description: Users may not be fully aware of how their health data is being analyzed, stored, and used to generate condition indicators displayed on the dashboard.
assumptions: Users may not understand the extent of data processing for health inference

title: Lack of user control over health data preferences
description: Users may lack control over how their health data is processed, what preferences they can set, or how long health indicators are retained.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing health data to generate risk signals may process more personal data than actually needed for the app's functional goals.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle requires processing only necessary data

title: Automated decision making on sensitive health data
description: The app uses automated analysis to infer health conditions (eating-disorder or diabetes risk), which may constitute automated decision-making on sensitive personal data without adequate safeguards.
assumptions: Health risk inference qualifies as automated decision-making on sensitive data under GDPR
